records.claim: The bank chooses the register with the highest cumulative usefulness (UT0+UT1+UT2) and scales its output by 2.5 when positive.
records.quote: Unlike the existing components, this component picks the digest of the most useful register among those available and forwards it to the second table.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Figure 5(c) specify selecting the most useful register among available registers in the bank.

records.claim: During training, exactly one available register per bank is randomly selected to update the tables with a single write port.
records.quote: If several registers were available within the same bank, it randomly selects one of them for the update.
records.why: Section 4.2 explicitly states that one available register per bank is randomly selected during training.

records.claim: The prediction algorithm evaluates the 8 banks independently, identifying registers belonging to each bank via stride-8 grouping.
records.quote: This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Figure 5(c) show bank 0 containing R0, R8, R16, ... R64, defining a stride-8 bank mapping.

records.claim: For each bank, usefulness weights from UT0, UT1, and UT2 are summed per register to pick the register with the maximum usefulness.
records.quote: Their outputs go to a Sigma producing "9 regs useful (skewed)".
records.why: Figure 5(c) shows summing UT0, UT1, and UT2 to find the most useful register in the bank.

records.claim: Outputs from all 8 banks are summed together to produce the final sR contribution.
records.quote: Below all eight banks: a final Sigma, output "sR".
records.why: Figure 5(c) shows a cross-bank summation node gathering all eight bank outputs into sR.

records.claim: The bank weight sum is multiplied by 2.5 if max_useful > 0, otherwise multiplied by 0.
records.open_question: Figure 5(c) labels the per-bank scaling block as 'x0 or x2.5', but the paper does not specify the exact gating condition or threshold that selects between x0 and x2.5.

records.claim: Training updates correlations only for logical registers that were available at prediction time.
records.quote: During training, we update the correlations only for logical registers that were available at prediction time.
records.why: Section 4.2 states verbatim that updates are restricted to registers available at prediction time.

records.claim: Each bank randomly selects one available register to update in order to maintain a single write port per table.
records.quote: Owing to this training method, each table in the register component also needs just a single write port.
records.why: Section 4.2 confirms that random single-register selection enables single write port tables.

records.claim: Usefulness weights in UT0, UT1, and UT2 are incremented if the bank weight table sum direction agreed with the outcome, and decremented otherwise.
records.open_question: Section 4.2 notes that the component includes a table tracking prediction usefulness, but does not specify the training update rule or agreement condition for usefulness counters.
